GRAPHIC REPRESENTATION OF EXTERNAL NOISE EXPOSURE
The attached figures show a graphical representation of the external noise exposure standards for new construction sites as explained in HUD Policy Circular 1390.2. The vertical line labeled NA (Normally Acceptable) represents noise levels of 45 dBA exceeded for more than 30 minutes per 24 hours; the vertical line labeled NU (Normally Unacceptable) represents noise levels of 65 dBA exceeded for more than 8 hours per 24 hours; and the vertical lines labeled U (Unacceptable) represent noise levels of 75 dBA exceeded for more than 8 hours per 24 hours, and noise levels of 80 dBA exceeded for more than 60 minutes per 24 hours. In use, the statistical distribution of the noise for a given location is superimposed on the figure and, if it crosses any of the vertical lines, it falls into that category.
Figures 1 through 3 present the analyses for three typical locations on the site. You will note from the three figures that, when the predicted noise curve just misses the bottom end of the vertical line labeled NU, it also clearly misses the two vertical lines labeled U. The slope of the curves was typical of the noise curves for all of the locations sampled and indicates that, if the noise level does not exceed 65 dBA for more than eight hours per 24 hours, the location falls in the Normally Acceptable category. In this case none of the noise curves cross the Unacceptable line.
